g.text: Infix to Prefix & Postfix Conversion: a + b * c / d - e
Dual string accumulation: Prefix = (op + v1 + v2) | Postfix = (v1 + v2 + op)
• Push a to both pre and post stacks; push '+' to op stack.
• Push b to both pre and post stacks.
• Incoming '*': prec('*')=2 > prec('+')=1 → strictly higher priority, no pop!
• Push '*' to op stack, then push c to both value stacks.
Both value stacks hold [a, b, c]. Operator stack holds [+, *].
See '/': Equal precedence to '*' triggers pop & combine, then push '/' and 'd'
• prec('/')=2 == prec('*')=2 → Equal priority! Pop op='*', v2='c', v1='b':
PRE: pre_frag = op + v1 + v2 = "* b c"
POST: post_frag = v1 + v2 + op = "b c *"
• Compare '/' vs new top '+': 2 > 1 → Push '/' to op stack: [+, /]
• Push d to both stacks: pre: [a, "*bc", d], post: [a, "bc*", d]
Sub-expressions "*bc" and "bc*" now treated as atomic operand values.
See '-': Cascading pop of '/' then '+', then push '-' and 'e'
• Compare '-' vs new top '+': prec('-')=1 == prec('+')=1 → Pop op='+', v2='/*bcd', v1='a':
• Op stack empty → push '-' : [-]. Push 'e' to value stacks.
End of string reached! Ready for final flushing.
End of String: Flush Remaining Operator '-' → Final Prefix & Postfix
on pop op: pre.push(op + v1 + v2); post.push(v1 + v2 + op); // Exact same operator stack precedence logic as infix evaluation!
